My practice is built around performance as a method — treating improvisation, notation, and live electronics not as separate disciplines but as aspects of a single enquiry.

I'm a composer, improviser, and electronic musician currently completing postgraduate study at the Royal Academy of Music, with a PhD beginning in September 2025 co-supervised by Rubens Askenar and Alex Hills.

My work moves between written composition and real-time improvisation, with a sustained interest in embodied listening, performer agency, and the conditions under which music comes into being. I'm drawn to music that keeps its process visible — where the gap between intention and sound is itself generative.

Alongside my own practice I work as an arranger and orchestrator with the City of Birmingham Symphony Orchestra, including projects for the BBC Proms at the Royal Albert Hall. I also teach musicianship at Junior Trinity and sing with the New London Chamber Choir.

Earlier training as a jazz guitarist at Trinity Laban continues to shape my approach to timbre and collaborative process — an openness to what the instrument and the room can offer.

PERFORMANCE

Live & Recorded
Guitar · Electronics
Tubular Bells · Voice
Performance is inseparable from composition in my practice. I perform regularly as a guitarist and electronic musician — in improvised settings, as a collaborator in contemporary works, and as part of the duo Red on Gold with violinist Anastasija Stanojevic.

I've performed at Music We'd Like to Hear, the 840 Series, MUSARC, and worked with the CBSO on BBC Proms projects at the Royal Albert Hall.
